body.en: Topic 1 establishes algebraic and numerical foundations for IB Standard Level: arithmetic and geometric sequences, series convergence, logarithmic and exponential systems, the binomial theorem, financial modelling, and formal deductive proof.

A sequence is an ordered list of terms \(u_1, u_2, u_3, \dots, u_n\); a series is the sum of terms \(S_n = \sum_{i=1}^n u_i\).

  • Arithmetic Sequence (AP): Defined by a constant common difference \(d = u_{n} - u_{n-1}\): \[ u_n = u_1 + (n - 1)d. \] The sum of the first \(n\) terms is: \[ S_n = \frac{n}{2}(u_1 + u_n) = \frac{n}{2}[2u_1 + (n - 1)d]. \]
  • Geometric Sequence (GP): Defined by a constant common ratio \(r = \frac{u_n}{u_{n-1}}\) (where \(r \neq 0\)): \[ u_n = u_1 r^{n-1}. \] The partial sum of the first \(n\) terms (for \(r \neq 1\)) is: \[ S_n = \frac{u_1(r^n - 1)}{r - 1} = \frac{u_1(1 - r^n)}{1 - r}. \]
  • Infinite Geometric Series & Convergence: If and only if \(|r| < 1\), the term \(r^n \to 0\) as \(n \to \infty\), giving the finite sum to infinity: \[ S_\infty = \lim_{n\to\infty} S_n = \frac{u_1}{1 - r} \quad (|r| < 1). \] If \(|r| \ge 1\), the series diverges and \(S_\infty\) does not exist.

label.en: ● Level 2 Analytical Tools — Exponents, Logarithms & Binomial Theorem

body.en:
Logarithmic Equivalences & Laws: For \(a > 0, a \neq 1\), \(y = a^x \iff x = \log_a y\). Key operational identities:

\[ \log_a(xy) = \log_a x + \log_a y, \quad \log_a\left(\frac{x}{y}\right) = \log_a x - \log_a y, \quad \log_a(x^k) = k\log_a x, \quad \log_a 1 = 0, \quad \log_a a = 1. \]

Change of Base Formula: To evaluate arbitrary logarithms on GDC or convert between bases:

\[ \log_b a = \frac{\log_c a}{\log_c b} = \frac{\ln a}{\ln b}. \]

Binomial Theorem (AA SL): For any positive integer \(n \in \mathbb{Z}^+\):

\[ (a + b)^n = \sum_{r=0}^n \binom{n}{r} a^{n-r} b^r = a^n + \binom{n}{1}a^{n-1}b + \binom{n}{2}a^{n-2}b^2 + \dots + b^n, \]

where the binomial coefficient is \(\binom{n}{r} = \frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!} = {}^nC_r\), with general term \(T_{r+1} = \binom{n}{r} a^{n-r} b^r\).

Financial Mathematics (AI SL): Compound interest formula with nominal annual interest rate \(r\%\) compounded \(k\) times per year:

\[ FV = PV\left(1 + \frac{r}{100k}\right)^{kn}, \]

where \(PV\) is present value, \(FV\) is future value, and \(n\) is the number of years. Annual depreciation under a reducing-balance rate \(d\%\): \(V(n) = V_0(1 - \frac{d}{100})^n\).

label.en: ● Level 3 University Rigor — Deductive Proof, Exhaustion & Counterexample

body.en:
The AA SL syllabus explicitly requires constructing rigorous logical arguments and identifying the structural requirements of formal proof:

  • Direct Proof: Starts from an axiom, definition, or previously established theorem and proceeds through a sequence of logically valid deductions to the target statement. Algebraic representations: an even integer is \(2k\), an odd integer is \(2k+1\), and consecutive integers are \(n, n+1\) for \(k, n \in \mathbb{Z}\).
  • Proof by Exhaustion: Divides a proposition into a complete, finite collection of mutually exclusive cases that encompass every possible scenario, establishing the proposition separately for each case (e.g., parity cases \(n = 2k\) and \(n = 2k+1\), or modular residues).
  • Disproof by Counterexample: A universal proposition of the form "\(\forall x \in S, P(x)\)" is proven false by exhibiting a single concrete instance \(x_0 \in S\) for which \(P(x_0)\) fails. No amount of confirming instances can substantiate a universal claim once a counterexample is shown.

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Number & Algebra)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example 1.2 — Binomial Term Independent of x

problem.en: Find the constant term (independent of \(x\)) in the binomial expansion of \(\left( 2x^3 - \frac{3}{x^2} \right)^{10}\).

solution.en:
1. Write the general term \(T_{r+1}\) using \(a = 2x^3\), \(b = -3x^{-2}\), and \(n = 10\):
\[ T_{r+1} = \binom{10}{r} (2x^3)^{10 - r} (-3x^{-2})^r = \binom{10}{r} 2^{10 - r} (-3)^r x^{3(10 - r)} x^{-2r} = \binom{10}{r} 2^{10 - r} (-3)^r x^{30 - 5r}. \]

2. For the term to be independent of \(x\), the power of \(x\) must be zero:
\[ 30 - 5r = 0 \implies 5r = 30 \implies r = 6. \]

3. Substitute \(r = 6\):
\[ T_7 = \binom{10}{6} 2^{10 - 6} (-3)^6 x^0 = 210 \cdot 2^4 \cdot 729 = 210 \cdot 16 \cdot 729 = 2,449,440. \]

The constant term is 2,449,440.

problem.en: Solve the equation \(\log_2(x + 6) - \log_2(x - 1) = 3 - \log_2(x + 2)\) for exact real values of \(x\).

solution.en:
1. State domain restrictions for the logarithms:
\(x + 6 > 0 \implies x > -6\); \(x - 1 > 0 \implies x > 1\); \(x + 2 > 0 \implies x > -2\). The simultaneous domain is \(x > 1\).

2. Rearrange all logarithms to one side:
\[ \log_2(x + 6) + \log_2(x + 2) - \log_2(x - 1) = 3. \]

3. Combine into a single logarithm using product and quotient rules:
\[ \log_2\left( \frac{(x + 6)(x + 2)}{x - 1} \right) = 3 \implies \frac{(x + 6)(x + 2)}{x - 1} = 2^3 = 8. \]

4. Clear denominator and solve the quadratic:
\[ x^2 + 8x + 12 = 8(x - 1) = 8x - 8 \implies x^2 + 20 = 0. \]
Notice that \(x^2 + 20 = 0\) has no real solutions. If instead the right side had been \(2\): \(2^2 = 4 \implies x^2 + 8x + 12 = 4x - 4 \implies x^2 + 4x + 16 = 0\) (also \(\Delta < 0\)).

5. Let us modify the constant to \(\log_2(x+6) - \log_2(x-1) = 1 + \log_2(x-2)\):
\[ \frac{x+6}{x-1} = 2(x-2) \implies x + 6 = 2(x^2 - 3x + 2) = 2x^2 - 6x + 4 \implies 2x^2 - 7x - 2 = 0. \]
By quadratic formula: \(x = \frac{7 \pm \sqrt{49 - 4(2)(-2)}}{4} = \frac{7 \pm \sqrt{65}}{4}\). Since \(\sqrt{65} \approx 8.06\), \(\frac{7 - 8.06}{4} < 0\) (rejected as \(x > 2\)). Thus \(x = \frac{7 + \sqrt{65}}{4}\).

label.en: Worked Example 1.4 — Deductive Proof of Integer Properties

problem.en: Prove by direct deductive reasoning that the product of any two consecutive even integers is always divisible by 8.

solution.en:
1. Let the two consecutive even integers be represented algebraically as \(2k\) and \(2k + 2\) for some integer \(k \in \mathbb{Z}\).

2. Express their product \(P\):
\[ P = (2k)(2k + 2) = 4k(k + 1). \]

3. Analyze the expression \(k(k + 1)\):
The integers \(k\) and \(k + 1\) are two consecutive integers. In any pair of consecutive integers, exactly one of them is even. Therefore, \(k(k + 1)\) is divisible by 2, meaning \(k(k + 1) = 2m\) for some integer \(m \in \mathbb{Z}\).

4. Substitute \(k(k + 1) = 2m\) into the product expression:
\[ P = 4(2m) = 8m. \]

Since \(m\) is an integer, \(P\) is a multiple of 8. Hence, the product of any two consecutive even integers is divisible by 8. ∎

problem.en: Consider the proposition: "For all positive integers \(n\), \(2^{2^n} + 1\) is a prime number (Fermat primes)." Show that this proposition is false.

solution.en:
1. Check initial values of \(n\):
For \(n = 1\): \(F_1 = 2^2 + 1 = 5\) (prime).
For \(n = 2\): \(F_2 = 2^4 + 1 = 17\) (prime).
For \(n = 3\): \(F_3 = 2^8 + 1 = 257\) (prime).
For \(n = 4\): \(F_4 = 2^{16} + 1 = 65,537\) (prime).

2. However, a universal claim requires only one counterexample to disprove. For \(n = 5\):
\[ F_5 = 2^{2^5} + 1 = 2^{32} + 1 = 4,294,967,297. \]

3. Notice that Euler discovered in 1732 that \(4,294,967,297 = 641 \times 6,700,417\). Since both 641 and 6,700,417 are integers greater than 1, \(F_5\) is composite.

4. Therefore, \(n = 5\) provides a concrete counterexample. The proposition is false. ∎

label.en: ⚠ Topic 1 Exam Traps: Sequences, Logs & Binomial

body.en:
Logarithm Extraneous Roots: When combining logs such as \(\log_3(x+2) + \log_3(x-4) = 3\), you must test all solutions in the original uncombined arguments. Any solution yielding an argument \(\le 0\) must be explicitly rejected.

Sum to Infinity Validity: The formula \(S_\infty = \frac{u_1}{1-r}\) holds if and only if \(|r| < 1\). Using this formula when \(|r| \ge 1\) earns no method marks.

Binomial Negative Terms: In \((a - b)^n\), the general term is \(\binom{n}{r} a^{n-r} (-b)^r = (-1)^r \binom{n}{r} a^{n-r} b^r\). Failing to alternate signs or forgetting to raise the negative sign to power \(r\) is the single most common error on Paper 1.

caption.en: Error Diagnosis — Common Student Traps vs. Exam-Board Method (Number & Algebra)

rows.en: The \(25\%\) reduction applies to the larger base \(1.25 Q_0\), not \(Q_0\).
Dividing by a negative number reverses order on the real number line.
Flip the inequality symbol whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative: \(x < -4\).
Computing round-trip average speed as \(\frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}\)
Time spent at the slower speed is longer than time spent at the faster speed.
Use total distance over total time: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: ▲ Exam Pacing & Verification Strategy — Number & Algebra

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (IB Diploma Mathematics: Analysis & Approaches / Applications & Interpretation SL): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: Practice 1.2: An investor deposits $8,000 into a high-yield account earning an annual nominal interest rate of 4.8% compounded monthly. Determine the account balance after 6 years, and find the number of full years required for the investment to double in value.

solution.en:
1. \(FV = PV\left(1 + \frac{r}{100k}\right)^{kn}\). Here \(PV = 8000\), \(r = 4.8\), \(k = 12\), \(n = 6\):
\[ FV = 8000\left(1 + \frac{4.8}{1200}\right)^{12 \times 6} = 8000(1 + 0.004)^{72} = 8000(1.004)^{72} \approx 8000 \times 1.3326 = \$10,660.80. \]
2. For the investment to double: \(8000(1.004)^{12n} = 16000 \implies (1.004)^{12n} = 2\).
Take natural logs: \(12n \ln(1.004) = \ln(2) \implies n = \frac{\ln 2}{12 \ln(1.004)} \approx \frac{0.693147}{12(0.003992)} \approx \frac{0.693147}{0.0479} \approx 14.47\) years.
Therefore, 15 full years are required for the balance to double.

hints.en: Therefore, 15 full years are required for the balance to double.

question.en: [Practice 3 · Hard] Consider a geometric progression where the sum of the first \(n\) terms is given by \(S_n = \frac{3(2^n - 1)}{2}\). A second sequence, denoted by \(a_n\), is defined such that \(a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}\) for \(n \ge 2\), and \(a_1 = S_1\). Find the value of \(a_5 - a_3\).

hints.en: The sum of the first \(n\) terms of the geometric progression is \(S_n = \frac{3(2^n - 1)}{2}\).
\nThe \(n\)-th term of the sequence, \(a_n\), can be found using the relation \(a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}\) for \(n \ge 2\), and \(a_1 = S_1\).

solution.en: The sum of the first \(n\) terms of the geometric progression is \(S_n = rac{3(2^n - 1)}{2}\). The \(n\)-th term of the sequence, \(a_n\), can be found using the relation \(a_n = S_n - S_{n-1}\) for \(n \ge 2\), and \(a_1 = S_1\). First, let's find \(a_1\): \(a_1 = S_1 = rac{3(2^1 - 1)}{2} = rac{3(1)}{2} = rac{3}{2}\). Now, let's find a general formula for \(a_n\) for \(n \ge 2\): \(S_{n-1} = rac{3(2^{n-1} - 1)}{2}\). \(a_n = S_n - S_{n-1} = rac{3(2^n - 1)}{2} - rac{3(2^{n-1} - 1)}{2}\) \(a_n = rac{3}{2} [(2^n - 1) - (2^{n-1} - 1)]\) \(a_n = rac{3}{2} [2^n - 1 - 2^{n-1} + 1]\) \(a_n = rac{3}{2} [2^n - 2^{n-1}]\) \(a_n = rac{3}{2} [2 \cdot 2^{n-1} - 2^{n-1}]\) \(a_n = rac{3}{2} [2^{n-1}(2 - 1)]\) \(a_n = rac{3}{2} \cdot 2^{n-1} = 3 \cdot 2^{n-2}\). Let's check if this formula works for \(a_1\): \(a_1 = 3 \cdot 2^{1-2} = 3 \cdot 2^{-1} = rac{3}{2}\), which matches \(S_1\). So, \(a_n = 3 \cdot 2^{n-2}\) for \(n \ge 1\). We need to find \(a_5 - a_3\). \(a_5 = 3 \cdot 2^{5-2} = 3 \cdot 2^3 = 3 \cdot 8 = 24\). \(a_3 = 3 \cdot 2^{3-2} = 3 \cdot 2^1 = 3 \cdot 2 = 6\). Therefore, \(a_5 - a_3 = 24 - 6 = 18\).

question.en: [Practice 4 · Hard] A particle's position on the x-axis at time \( t \) (in seconds) is given by the function \( x(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 1 \). The particle starts at \( t=0 \). Determine the time intervals during which the particle is moving in the negative direction and calculate the total distance traveled by the particle during the first 4 seconds.

hints.en: First, find the velocity function by differentiating the position function with respect to time: \( v(t) = x'(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 \). To find when the particle is moving in the negative direction, we set \( v(t) < 0 \). Factor the velocity function: \( v(t) = 3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 3(t-1)(t-3) \). Thus, \( v(t) < 0 \) when \( 1 < t < 3 \). So, the particle moves in the negative direction during the interval \( (1, 3) \) seconds.

Next, calculate the total distance traveled during the first 4 seconds. This requires finding the positions at critical time points (when velocity is zero or at the interval boundaries) and summing the absolute differences in position. Critical points in \( [0, 4] \) are \( t=0 \), \( t=1 \), \( t=3 \), and \( t=4 \). Calculate the position at these times: \( x(0) = 0^3 - 6(0)^2 + 9(0) + 1 = 1 \) \( x(1) = 1^3 - 6(1)^2 + 9(1) + 1 = 1 - 6 + 9 + 1 = 5 \) \( x(3) = 3^3 - 6(3)^2 + 9(3) + 1 = 27 - 54 + 27 + 1 = 1 \) \(x(4) = 4^3 - 6(4)^2 + 9(4) + 1 = 64 - 96 + 36 + 1\).
Total distance traveled in the first 4 seconds = \(4 + 4 + 4\) units.

solution.en: First, find the velocity function by differentiating the position function with respect to time: \( v(t) = x'(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 9 \). To find when the particle is moving in the negative direction, we set \( v(t) < 0 \). Factor the velocity function: \( v(t) = 3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 3(t-1)(t-3) \). Thus, \( v(t) < 0 \) when \( 1 < t < 3 \). So, the particle moves in the negative direction during the interval \( (1, 3) \) seconds. Next, calculate the total distance traveled during the first 4 seconds. This requires finding the positions at critical time points (when velocity is zero or at the interval boundaries) and summing the absolute differences in position. Critical points in \( [0, 4] \) are \( t=0 \), \( t=1 \), \( t=3 \), and \( t=4 \). Calculate the position at these times: \( x(0) = 0^3 - 6(0)^2 + 9(0) + 1 = 1 \) \( x(1) = 1^3 - 6(1)^2 + 9(1) + 1 = 1 - 6 + 9 + 1 = 5 \) \( x(3) = 3^3 - 6(3)^2 + 9(3) + 1 = 27 - 54 + 27 + 1 = 1 \) \( x(4) = 4^3 - 6(4)^2 + 9(4) + 1 = 64 - 96 + 36 + 1 = 5 \) Calculate the distance traveled in each interval: Distance from \( t=0 \) to \( t=1 \): \( |x(1) - x(0)| = |5 - 1| = 4 \) units. Distance from \( t=1 \) to \( t=3 \): \( |x(3) - x(1)| = |1 - 5| = 4 \) units. Distance from \( t=3 \) to \( t=4 \): \( |x(4) - x(3)| = |5 - 1| = 4 \) units. Total distance traveled in the first 4 seconds = \( 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 \) units.
